cv.assignment: sort component IDs, NumPy default_rng(seed) permutation, then np.array_split into four balanced component folds
cv.bootstrap_unit: paired component resampling, conditional on the four fixed cross-fit models
cv.fit_rule: fit each fold model on the other 24 components; predict every row of its eight held-out components with targets and masks disabled

raw_plus_clock.features: current raw inputs plus frozen scalar CUSUM clock

raw_plus_group_states.features: current raw inputs plus three fast/slow state features for each of 13 groups

features.ema_initialization: both EMA states initialize from the first post-warmup group-energy observation; each row updates state with that row before emitting its features
features.filter: independent scalar random-walk Kalman filter per standardized input channel
features.group_energy: mean squared clipped standardized innovation within each of the 13 fixed input groups
features.innovation: pre-update residual divided by sqrt(predicted state variance + R), clipped to [-8, 8]
features.inputs_to_transform: features only; no target, scoring mask, sequence identifier, or future row
features.reference_scalar_clock: the frozen all-channel CUSUM clock from innovation_clock_r1, appended to raw inputs only in the reference arm
features.sequence_reset: Kalman and EMA states initialize independently inside every sequence
features.warmup_normalization: per-sequence mean and sample standard deviation on input rows 0..98; scale floor 1e-6

grading.claim_limit: No endpoint, student, competition validation, public leaderboard, online target-feedback, or long-sequence generalization claim.
grading.labels_and_masks: read only by the separate grader after all label-blind OOF predictions and their hashes are frozen
grading.negative_result: Defer this exact fast/slow linear representation but retain other causal Kalman state encodings and recurrent interactions as open hypotheses.
grading.primary: pooled OOF official weighted Pearson score over the held-out component predictions
grading.success: Group-state arm has a repeatable practical increment over raw across the four folds and component resampling, sufficient to justify a small recurrent representation test; a tiny/noisy linear delta alone is not a B300 direction.
grading.uncertainty: Bootstrap conditions on one fixed 32-component fit-side sample and its four CV fits; it does not include training-seed, sequence-selection, clean-validation, or public-transfer uncertainty.

model.intercept: weighted target mean minus weighted feature mean dot unstandardized coefficients
model.kind: two-output weighted standardized ridge linear model
model.sample_weight: abs(clip(y[t], -2, 2)), separately per target, matching the official metric's label weights
model.standardization: weighted fit-sample mean and standard deviation using stable centered weighted batch moments; feature scales floored at 1e-6
model.target_alignment: same input row x[t] to target y[t] for t >= 99

question: Do causal groupwise fast/slow Kalman-innovation energy states add held-out predictive signal beyond the current 112 raw inputs, and does a single scalar innovation clock add any linear signal as a reference?

resources.profile_source: research/campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/causal_label_proxy_r1/profile_receipt_r1.json (same Parquet reader and weighted-ridge family at 1.5 GB); a separate exact-feature one-sequence profile is required before the full cross-fit fit

selection.exposure: Previously inspected fit-side development sample. Four-fold component cross-fitting is internal incrementality evidence only, not a fresh validation split.
selection.fit_membership: one complete row group from each of 32 distinct fold0.fit.train components; no valid, test, or evaluation group is read

sample_source.selection: the exact 32 complete component groups previously used in the feature-only innovation-clock screen; all are in fold0.fit.train and have already been exposed during development

why_it_might_work: The scalar CUSUM clock reached its cap early and collapsed distinct channel families. Per-group fast and slow exponentially weighted innovation energies may preserve local surprise and persistence at different timescales while retaining the raw inputs.
